title: Cutover leaves SYA.nudgeSplit at 0 — new nudge pot is repointed but never refunded by the StableYieldAccumulator claim path (incomplete migration)
description: The predecessor stop-gap DisableNudgeAndDivertDonations cut funding to the exploited BatchNFTMinter by setting SYA.setNudgeSplit(0) (its PRIMARY lever — the SYA.claim() path routes nudgeSplit% of each claim's USDC to SYA.nudge). ReplaceBatchNFTMinter is the script that is meant to supersede that stop-gap: it repoints SYA.nudge = newMinter and pooler.batchMinter = newMinter, and one-time-seeds ~50.4 USDC into the new pot. But it never restores SYA.nudgeSplit. Verified live on the fork: SYA.nudgeSplit() == 0 before the run, and the script issues no setNudgeSplit call (full trace inspected — only setNudgeAddress is called on SYA). So after the cutover the new minter is fully wired yet receives 0% of every subsequent claim. The script's own stated purpose ("repoint its two real funders ... so the nudge works again") is only half-achieved: the pointer is restored but the split that makes the pointer meaningful is left at the stop-gap value.
impact: The new BatchNFTMinter nudge incentive is funded only by the single ~50.4 USDC bootstrap seed and never replenished through the SYA claim path. The nudge feature (count >= nudgeSize=40 triggers a full-balance payout) is effectively dead after the seed is consumed, defeating the purpose of redeploying the fixed minter. No funds are lost, but the migrated mechanism is non-functional going forward until a separate owner-only setNudgeSplit(N) tx is sent. This is a silent post-migration availability gap: the script reports success, mainnet-addresses.ts is rewritten, and an operator reading the logs would believe the cutover is complete.
attackPath: Predecessor stop-gap DisableNudgeAndDivertDonations set SYA.setNudgeSplit(0) to cut funding to the exploited minter.
ReplaceBatchNFTMinter (the supersede script) repoints SYA.nudge = newMinter and pooler.batchMinter = newMinter and seeds ~50.4 USDC.
Script never calls SYA.setNudgeSplit(N) — verified live: only setNudgeAddress is issued.
SYA.claim() routes nudgeSplit% (=0) to nudge, so nudgeAmount=0 forever.
Script reports success, mainnet-addresses.ts rewritten — operator believes cutover is complete while the nudge feature is dead after the seed.
recommendation: Add an explicit SYA.setNudgeSplit(<intended %>) call to _repoint() (sourcing the intended split — e.g. the pre-stop-gap 30% — from the operator/spec per Configuration Safety), plus a post-condition require(SYA.nudgeSplit() == intended, "nudgeSplit not restored"). If restoring the split is intentionally deferred to a separate broadcast, the script header and progress JSON must say so explicitly so the cutover is not mistaken for complete.
evidence: Fork preview (block ~25207560) ran successfully with no setNudgeSplit call; on-chain reads at block 25207599: SYA.nudgeSplit()==0, SYA.nudge()==0x4ef0...41f3 (old) pre-run; post-run trace sets SYA.nudge=newMinter but nudgeSplit untouched. DisableNudgeAndDivertDonations.s.sol lines 132-137 perform the setNudgeSplit(0) this script fails to reverse. StableYieldAccumulator.claim() lines 506-516: nudge funding gated entirely by nudgeSplit; at 0, nudgeAmount=0 (confirmed at src L506 `if (nudgeSplit > 0 && nudge == address(0)) revert` and L512 `nudgeAmount = (actualPayment * nudgeSplit) / 100`).

tests.name: test_BMR_M_01_nudgeSplitZero_claimFundsNudgeWithZero
tests.proves: Real SYA claim pulls 9.537478 USDC; nudge-pot funding delta == 0 with nudgeSplit==0 after the script's setNudgeAddress repoint.

tests.name: test_BMR_M_01_contrast_withSetNudgeSplit_potIsFunded
tests.proves: Same path with the missing setNudgeSplit(30) routes exactly 7.430881 USDC == 30% of 24.769604 USDC payment, confirming nudgeSplit is the lever the cutover fails to restore.

poc.scopeNote: Fully VALID. All tests pass against pinned fork block 25207560 using real on-chain contracts.
